title: Form Tag
body:
`<form>` — groups input controls and defines how their values get sent to the server.

```HTML
<form action="URL" method=GET>
	<label>Email</label>
	<input type=text name=email>
</form>
```

`action` is the [[URL]] the data is submitted to, and `method` is the [[HTTP Verb]] used. With `GET` the values are appended to the URL as a [[Query String]] — visible in the address bar, in history and in logs, so never for passwords. With `POST` they go in the request body instead.

Only controls with a `name` attribute are submitted; the name becomes the key and the control's current value becomes the value. Submitting a form triggers a full page navigation by default, which is why JavaScript-driven pages call `event.preventDefault()` on the submit handler and send the data with [[Fetch]] instead.

See [[Input Tag]] for the controls that go inside one.
